title: Parameterized naturality of evaluation on an arrow family
statement:
Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and coherent transformations of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the coherent nerve $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ of Kan complexes of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. All objects fit in fixed containing universes. Let $C$ be a $\mathcal W$-small quasicategory, $F,G:C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ coherent functors, $a\in C$ and $\eta\in F(a)$ a vertex. Put $T=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})}(F,G)$ and $M_x=\operatorname{Map}^{R}_C(a,x)$. Let $j_x:M_x\times\Delta^1\to C$ be the right-pinch arrow family of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Apply $F$ to $j_x$ and precompose with $\eta$ to form a coherent cocone $\Delta_{M_x}*\to\Delta_{M_x}F(x)$; denote its point map by $e^F_{\eta,x}:M_x\to F(x)$, up to homotopy, using the point-family equivalence of [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion]. Evaluation of transformations and the analogous $G$-action give two maps, interpreted through that same point-family equivalence,
$$T\times M_x\longrightarrow G(x),\qquad (\alpha,f)\longmapsto\alpha_x(e^F_{\eta,x}(f)),\qquad (\alpha,f)\longmapsto G(f)(\alpha_a(\eta)).$$
These maps are simplicially homotopic. The homotopy is compatible with all simplicial parameters of the coherent transformation and arrow families: for every simplicial parameter $B\to T$, it restricts to the corresponding homotopy on $B\times M_x$, with all faces, degeneracies and higher naturality compatibilities in $x$ retained by internal evaluation on $C$. No representability or invertibility hypothesis on $e^F_{\eta,x}$, and no Yoneda evaluation equivalence, is assumed.

proof.text: Work in a containing universe large enough for $C$, $\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$, its functor category $D=\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal W})$, and all parameter objects below. By [lem-coef-kan-coherent-nerve-quasicategory] the target is a quasicategory, and [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes $D$ a quasicategory. The right-pinch comparisons of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] therefore apply to both $C$ and $D$. Put $P=T\times M_x$. Use the homotopy equivalences $\beta_{X,Y}:\operatorname{Fun}(X,Y)\to U_{\mathcal S}(X,Y)$ of [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification]. Their statement supplies compatibility with composition and evaluation at a point on full parameter spaces. We use this precise comparison, not an arbitrary equivalence between mapping-space models. Its containing-universe clause permits the parameter $P$ even if $T$ is not $\mathcal W$-small; the endpoint spaces remain the given $\mathcal W$-small Kan complexes.

source.place: Preparation: internal functor objects and the point-family comparison; Kerodon 03M4 and 038A fix the evaluation convention.

proof.text:
The definitions in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] give a simplicial evaluation map $\operatorname{ev}:D\times C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$: on an $n$-simplex $(h,c)$, evaluate $h:C\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W}$ on $(c,\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^n})$. Let $k:T\times\Delta^1\to D$ be the universal right-pinch family for $(F,G)$ and $j:M_x\times\Delta^1\to C$ the stipulated family for $(a,x)$. Form the single map
$$Q:P\times\Delta^1_u\times\Delta^1_v\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal W},\qquad Q(t,m,u,v)=\operatorname{ev}(k(t,v),j(m,u)).$$
Its four corner restrictions, in order $(0,0),(1,0),(0,1),(1,1)$, are constant at $A=F(a), B=F(x), A'=G(a), B'=G(x)$. Its bottom, right, left and top sides are respectively the full families $F(j)$, $\alpha_x$, $\alpha_a$, $G(j)$. This follows by substituting the two endpoint restrictions of $k$ and $j$; the formula is a simplicial map because evaluation and both pinch families are simplicial maps.

source.place: Agent-written universal naturality square from internal evaluation; Kerodon 03M4.

proof.text:
Restrict $Q$ to the two monotone triangles of $\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$. Their vertex lists are $((0,0),(1,0),(1,1))$ and $((0,0),(0,1),(1,1))$. Thus they give maps $h_0:P\to V(A,B,B')$ and $h_1:P\to V(A,A',B')$ in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Both long-edge restrictions are exactly the same map $d:P\to U(A,B')$, the diagonal of $Q$. Write $\mu$ for the composition class on the arrow spaces, obtained from that node's right-pinched composition using $j$. Its characterization gives
$$[\mu(\alpha_x,F(j))]=[\ell][\theta]^{-1}[\theta h_0]=[\ell h_0]=[d],$$
$$[\mu(G(j),\alpha_a)]=[\ell][\theta]^{-1}[\theta h_1]=[\ell h_1]=[d].$$
Here every equation is between maps out of the entire $P$, not separate equations at its vertices. The homotopies are obtained by precomposing the homotopy inverse equation for $\theta$ with $h_i$ and postcomposing with $\ell$. Hence the square has compared the two composites on the full transformation and arrow parameters.

source.place: Construction 4.6.8.9: triangle restriction characterizes composition; apply to the two explicitly listed triangles of the naturality square.

proof.text:
Choose representatives, using $\beta^{-1}$ from [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification], of the four side families:
$$p:M_x\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,B),\quad q:M_x\to\operatorname{Fun}(A',B'),\quad r:T\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,A'),\quad s:T\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,B').$$
Each has its specified comparison homotopy to the corresponding side of $Q$. Pull them to $P$. The composition clause of that node turns Step 3 into
$$[s(t)\circ p(m)]=[q(m)\circ r(t)]\quad\text{as maps }P\to\operatorname{Fun}(A,B').$$
Indeed postcomposition with the homotopy equivalence $\beta_{A,B'}$ carries the two displayed maps to the two composites already compared in Step 3; composing with its homotopy inverse cancels it. Postcompose this homotopy-class equality with the simplicial evaluation map $\operatorname{ev}_{\eta}:\operatorname{Fun}(A,B')\to B'$. It becomes
$$[\,(t,m)\mapsto s(t)(p(m)(\eta))\,]=[\,(t,m)\mapsto q(m)(r(t)(\eta))\,].$$
No inverse to an action map $M_x\to F(x)$ has been used.

source.place: Kerodon 038A and 03M4: compose the full mapping-space comparison with evaluation at the given point.

proof.text: Identify these two maps with the maps in the statement. The family $F(j)$ is the bottom side of $Q$. Its precomposition with the constant point $\eta:*\to A$ is the stipulated cocone. By the precomposition-by-a-point and constant-diagram clauses of [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification], its point map is $m\mapsto p(m)(\eta)$, up to homotopy, under exactly the point-family equivalence of [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion]. Thus this is $e^F_{\eta,x}$. The right side corresponds to $s(t)$, so the first map of Step 4 is $\alpha_x(e^F_{\eta,x}(m))$. Similarly $r(t)(\eta)$ is evaluation of the transformation at $(a,\eta)$, and the top side corresponds to $q(m)$; the second map is therefore $G(m)(\alpha_a(\eta))$. These identifications use the full-family comparison, including its composition homotopies. They are not inferred merely from equality on vertices.

source.place: Kerodon 038A action on a point and 03M4 evaluation; apply the specified point-family equivalence.

proof.text: The homotopy-class calculation yields an actual simplicial homotopy of the two maps $P\to G(x)$. More explicitly, the comparison homotopies, the two triangle homotopies and their inverses give a finite edge zigzag in $\operatorname{Fun}(P,G(x))$. This is Kan by [lem-cbc-kan-functor-space-kan], since $G(x)$ is Kan and all objects fit in our containing universe. Reverse an edge by filling a $2$-horn whose other given edge is the degenerate identity; compose consecutive edges by filling an inner $2$-horn. Repeating these operations gives one edge with the required endpoints. By the internal-functor definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], that edge is a map $P\times\Delta^1\to G(x)$ with precisely the two required endpoint restrictions. This construction also covers $P=\varnothing$.

source.place: Agent-written compression of the finite homotopy zigzag using the Kan horn condition.

proof.text: Retain the square $Q$ and its two triangles as the coherent witness, rather than discarding them after passing to homotopy classes. For any $b:B_0\to T$ the entire witness is its restriction along $b\times\operatorname{id}_{M_x}$: explicitly it is $\operatorname{ev}(k(b(-),v),j(-,u))$. The homotopy of Step 6 restricts along this same map, so no new vertexwise choices are made for $B_0$. Faces and degeneracies of $b$ are just further precompositions. For the asserted higher compatibilities in $x$, evaluation was defined on all of $D\times C$ in Step 2. Given any simplex $\sigma:\Delta^n\to C$, its restriction is the same map $\operatorname{ev}(k(-,v),\sigma(-))$; restricting $\sigma$ along $\delta:[m]\to[n]$ gives exactly $\operatorname{ev}(k(-,v),\sigma\delta(-))$. Pulling back this identity to the arrow families gives the higher naturality data of $Q$. Composition retains these faces and degeneracies by [lem-cbc-simplicial-composition-spine], and the point-family comparison retains all additional simplicial parameters by [lem-coef-point-family-q-counit-identification]. Consequently the homotopy is furnished with these coherent compatibilities, rather than merely a collection of objectwise equations. This establishes every parameter clause without representability or a Yoneda theorem.
